target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: papillose FLOPO:0991059 – tuberculate FLOPO:0991060)
reason: A compound of two existing FLOPO values, written like 'linear-lanceolate'. It is modelled as a continuum between the two values, not as a new term.
Half-clasping the stem. PATO_0104363 is defined as 'at least partially enclosing an axis', which covers it, and the FLOPO amplexicaul class is obsolete in favour of it.
The quality is acuminate; 'bluntly' and 'short' only modify it and are dropped, as with other degree modifiers.
'With dark lines' on a corolla or seed means marked with narrow lines of another colour, which is FLOPO streaked. One example ('or dark lines in the cup') is a fragment.
Decurving pedicels and spikes bend downwards. PATO drooping is defined as 'bending or hanging downwards'; recurved (backward or inward) is the wrong direction.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum of two values: spherical PATO_0001499 – campanulate PATO_0104350)
reason: A compound of two existing shape values, which is handled by the continuum pattern rather than a term.
Caulescent = with an evident stem, as in the previous rule C344 for 'caulescent'. 'Long' is a size modifier with no value and is dropped.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: scalloped PATO_0001889 [crenate], approximately per docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md – serrated PATO_0001206)
reason: A compound of two margin values, with 'sub-' marking the first as approximate. Two patterns cover it; no term is needed.
A truncation of 'indumentum dense'. The quality is dense, and its bearer is the part's indumentum (FLOPO_0986003), not the part itself.
'Widest about or below the middle' gives where the bearer's greatest width lies along its length. This is the open 'position of greatest width' pattern from the 2026-11-14 review, not a term.
Veins 'distinguishable' are clearly visible, as in rule C176 for 'distinct'. 'Not distinguishable' then falls to inconspicuous PATO_0000464 by negation.

target: new: colour admixture (tinged), accepted concept FLOPO-PATTERN:colour_transition in curation/botanical_concept_proposals.tsv, with orange (PATO_0000953)
reason: 'Tinged' is a weak admixture of a named colour. The curator decided on 2026-09-18 to model it as a composition rather than an atomic term for each colour.
A connective 'without extension' is not prolonged beyond the thecae, i.e. it has no connective appendage. The bract example is unclear and should not use this rule.
Palmate venation means three or more primary veins radiating from one point, which is PATO actinodromous (Hickey). The vein count in '3(-5)-nerved' goes to docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md.
Spatheate = provided with a spathe, and the bearer class exists. FLOPO:0991222 spathaceous is a different quality: resembling a spathe.

A fern part (reduced, modified basal pinnae), not a quality, and neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for it. Mapping it to leaflet PO_0020049 would make 'aphlebia absent' false; a bearer class should be proposed separately.
A misspelling of buttressed; the class exists and its listed bearers include the stem and the whole plant.
A prefix split off 'pseudo-indusium' and 'pseudo-petiole': a transcription fragment, not a quality.

target: new: two values of two attributes in one word (sericeous PATO_0104358 + white PATO_0000323 of the hairs)
reason: The word means covered in silky hairs that are white. It splits into an indumentum value and a hair colour, and neither half needs a new term.
Bell-like = bell-shaped, which is an exact synonym of PATO campanulate.
'Divided almost to the base' gives the depth of the incision. This is the open 'depth and order of division' pattern from the 2026-11-14 review.

target: new: colour admixture (tinged/flushed), accepted concept FLOPO-PATTERN:colour_transition, with bronze (PATO_0002363)
reason: 'Flushed' is a weak admixture of a named colour, the same as 'tinged'. It is composed with the existing bronze value.

The colour is stated: the bearer is grey, and 'darker' compares it with an unnamed part. Bare 'darker' was rejected earlier because it gave no colour; here the comparison is dropped and the colour kept.
An inflorescence that is 'mostly male' has mostly staminate flowers. This is a quality of the whole towards its parts, with a frequency qualifier.
'Nipped in below the mouth' means narrowed or constricted; the glume and lemma examples are truncated.

label: clathrate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a scale by virtue of the scale's cells having thick, dark radial walls and thin, clear outer walls, so that the scale appears latticed like a window. NOTE: Pteridology; the statements seen are negations ('not clathrate') and use rule:negated_value once the class exists.
reason: A standard character of fern rhizome scales with no PATO or FLOPO term; it is needed before 'not clathrate' can be negated.
The definition of FLOPO lyrate already says 'pinnately lobed or divided, with a large terminal lobe', so 'pinnate-' adds nothing.
Raphides are not a part (decision in flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv); the cells that hold them are idioblasts. 'Packed' (abundance) is lost in this mapping.
'Without a mucro' = not mucronate. Mucro has no bearer class, so the negation of the existing value is used.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1, part of the bearer (margin), with red (PATO_0000322)
reason: The colour belongs to the margin of the part, not the whole part. It is the existing red value restricted by the part-of-the-bearer slot.
